Money is moving onto the internet, and the shift has a name: Open Money. This is money that is open, portable, agentic, and owned by you. MetaMask spent the last ten years building it; with 100M+ downloads, users in ~190 countries, and trillions in cumulative transaction volume, it's the most trusted self-custodial financial platform on the internet. Now we're building the operating system for your money: one place to hold, move, grow, and use anything you own.  Join a remote-first, global team rebuilding how money works: a problem that touches everyone, every day.
About MetaMask & Trade

MetaMask is a self-custodial wallet used by tens of millions of people. In Trade, people swap, bridge, trade perps, predict and earn. Core UX is the part of MetaMask mobile that sit inside: Home, the navigation, balances, tokens and positions, and the path from the first screen into each of them.

People open the app and land on Home. If that screen is slow, crowded, or unclear about what to do next, Swap, Perps, Predict and Earn see fewer of the people who opened the app. The surface is live. You start from the app people already have, and you keep shipping on it.

The role is Staff Product Manager, Core UX. You write the vision for Home and the navigation, and you run the build with design and engineering. A design background is a requirement, because the work is the screen itself.

The Role

You are the product manager for Core UX on MetaMask mobile. You own the vision, the roadmap and the backlog for Home and the navigation, and you own whether that screen is working.

You will work closely with:

• The Core UX engineering team

• Design

• Data and analytics

• The product managers for Swap, Perps, Predict and Earn

Those products show up on Home. You own how a person reaches them from there, and how their balances and positions show up. Their roadmaps stay with their product managers. Yours is Home and the navigation.

The app is already live and people open it every day, so you start from what is there. You walk design leadership through the screen, and you are in the reviews where the layout gets decided.

What You'll Do

Set the Core UX vision

Write what Home is for, who has to succeed on it, and what it shows before anyone taps. Getting back to an open position has to be fast for people who already trade here. A first install still has to reach one real action in that same session.

Write down where a MetaMask person would already know what to tap, and where one of those apps does something we should study. Then write the roadmap, with the tradeoffs and the order, and what each step changes on Home.

Own Home, the navigation and the defaults

Own what a person sees when they open the app. That is balances, tokens and positions, and the way into Swap, Perps, Predict and Earn. A balance, a token, a position and an entry point are different, and Home has to show each one in a place the person can find.

Decide what Home shows before anyone taps. Anything past that waits until the person opens it. Put Swap, Perps and Predict close together for people who use more than one of them. A person using only one of those products still has to be able to finish their action.

Search and any assistance that sits on Home are part of this surface. You specify what stays on the screen, and what the person still confirms before money moves.

Get people to a first action, and get them to come back

You own the first session and the return after it. Count how many new wallets take a real action, and how many of those people open the app again. Define the path from the open to a confirmed action, and instrument it.

Review screens with design

You have a design background, and the role uses it. You review screens for hierarchy, type, spacing and what a tap does. You mark up a screen and say what should change, in writing, so design and engineering can build from the note.

You write the product point of view clearly enough that design and engineering can build it. You are in the design reviews. A crowded screen, or a tap that does the wrong thing, gets the specific change you want.

Work with the products that live on Home

Each MetaMask trade primitive already has their own product manager. You own the entry from Home and the way their positions and balances read there. When a change to Home helps one product and hurts another, you name the tradeoff in the spec.

You coordinate the sequencing when a Home change depends on one of those teams, or when one of their launches depends on Home. The spec says what Home will show on the day their change ships.

Run the work

You take a problem through spec, design, build, test and launch, and then you read what happened. You run planning and the backlog with the Core UX engineering team.

A feature is done when the edge cases are handled, the screen is fast enough to use, and we can see the result in the data. That includes an empty Home, a person who uses one product, and a person who uses several.

When something breaks, you write down what happened and what we will change in the screen or in the process, so the same break has a fix.

Who You Are

You have owned the main screen of a consumer product people open every day, and you stayed on it through launch. You can set a direction for that screen and stay with the tickets until it ships.

You:

• Mark up a screen and say what the tap should do.

• Know which KPI a given screen is supposed to impact, and tell a real move from noise.

• Write a short spec that engineering and design can build, and use that same note when you walk a director through the decision.

• Sit with someone who already uses the app and someone who just installed, and turn what they do into the next change on Home.

• Work on a live product, where the screen is already open and the next change has to ship on top of it.

Don't meet all the requirements? Don't sweat it. We’re passionate about building a diverse team of humans and as such, if you think you've got what it takes for our chaotic-but-fun, remote-friendly, start-up environment—apply anyway, detailing your relevant transferable skills in your cover letter. Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

This is a remote position and we're considering candidates in the UK, Spain or Ireland.

The Opportunity

About our platform

Grafana Cloud moves millions of metrics, log lines, and traces per second from our customers' environments into a highly available, low-latency stack that processes and stores this data, and serves it to dashboards and alerting tools. We aim to grow this to hundreds of millions per second, and it's critical that as we grow, we improve our performance, increase our reliability, and do it efficiently and securely.

The Foundations department owns the Internal Engineering Platform (IEP): the Kubernetes clusters, cloud service provider resources (CSP), hardware, identity, delivery, and observability systems that Grafana Labs's application engineers use to build, deploy, and run their workloads.

About the Infrastructure group

We're hiring an engineering manager for the Foundations Infrastructure group, which owns the cloud infrastructure Grafana Cloud runs on. The group provisions and operates Kubernetes clusters and CSP resources across GCP, AWS, and Azure; enforces identity, access, and security controls across those environments; and runs the observability and cost-visibility systems that keep the infrastructure measurable and accountable.

You'll lead one of the squads of platform engineers that comprise the group.

We're platform engineers, and our application teams are our users. Our job is to give them leverage: self-service building blocks that take care of the hard parts of infrastructure, so they can focus on what they're building. We treat the platform as a product and value the experience of the people who use it. When a change is well communicated and understood, teams welcome it, and it lands as an improvement that makes the right way the easy way. You'll lead a squad that makes that happen.

How we work

Foundations is a global team that works asynchronously. The people who own a component or problem make the decisions about it, once stakeholders have had a chance to weigh in. Application teams build and run their own services; we give them a self-service platform to do it on.

Every engineer is on-call for the components their squad provides. We plan on-call, tactical work, and time off into every quarter, so roadmap work is roughly half of an engineer's time rather than all of it.

What You'll Be Doing

• Hire, manage, and develop a squad of platform engineers, with regular feedback and career conversations that support each person's growth.

• Own your squad's roadmap and quarterly objectives: help decide what the squad works on, what it defers, and why, across a broad remit where demand always exceeds capacity.

• Take platform changes from design to fleet-wide adoption: staged rollouts, migration paths, and clear communication, so changes land well for the teams who depend on them.

• Partner with the other Infrastructure squads on work that spans them, and with the teams across Foundations and the rest of Engineering whose work depends on yours.

• Help shape how the group works as a whole, including planning, on-call, and the ownership model between squads.

• Own the squad's intake. Requests, reviews, and support from application teams arrive continuously; keep them triaged and visible so that planned work still moves.

• Keep on-call healthy: ensure a sustainable load and support incident response.

• Work across team boundaries, contributing beyond your squad's scope where Foundations needs it.

We invest heavily in developer productivity. You can use modern AI coding assistants as part of your daily workflow (your choice of tools, within security guidelines), backed by a company-funded usage budget so you can iterate quickly without unnecessary friction.

We encourage pragmatic AI-assisted development: faster prototyping, test generation, refactors, documentation, and incident follow-ups, always paired with strong code review and quality standards.

What Makes You a Great Fit

• Experience managing engineers, ideally a team that builds and operates production CSP infrastructure, security, networking and/or storage

• Hands-on depth in at least one area of platform engineering, such as cloud infrastructure and Kubernetes, infrastructure security and access, or observability. You can challenge a design in your area on its merits, and the engineers on your team will expect you to.

• Fluency with infrastructure as code and with running Kubernetes in production.

• A track record of landing internal engineering/developer platform changes at scale. You've driven a migration or a rollout across many teams or many clusters, and you know what makes one stall.

• The ability to explain platform engineering to very different audiences (platform engineers, application teams, product management and business leadership) and to make the case for what the squad should and shouldn't take on.

• Be comfortable collaborating across time zones and cultures in a fully remote environment, using clear, written communication to build trust and psychological safety.

• You're a motivated self-starter with a strong bias toward action and ownership, able to navigate ambiguity in a complex problem space.

• Comfort with AI-assisted tooling. We embrace AI and agentic development, so we expect you to be curious and comfortable using AI-powered tools, and ideally to have practical experience folding them into a team's workflow.

Bonus Points For

• Experience across more than one of the group's areas: cloud infrastructure, infrastructure security, and observability

• Hands-on depth in cloud infrastructure security: cloud IAM, Kubernetes security, secrets, and workload identity on at least one major cloud provider. You can challenge a threat model or an access design on its merits, and the engineers on your team will expect you to.

• Building self-service infrastructure for application teams

• Running observability for a production platform at scale

• Operating across more than one of GCP, AWS, and Azure

• You've worked in or on open source, or other community-based projects. At Grafana Labs, "OSS is in our DNA"

• Understanding of dependency injection, Spring configuration, application lifecycle, and exception handling.

2. Microservices & System Design

• Understanding of scalable and resilient microservices architecture.
• Knowledge of service-to-service communication, API design, failure handling, retries, timeouts, and fault tolerance.

• Ability to identify edge cases and make sensible engineering trade-offs.

We are looking for a Buisness Development Representative, Consultant & Broker Channels (BDR, Consultant & Broker) to join our sales team. The Business Development Representative, Consultant & Broker Channels is responsible for expanding and strengthening the organization's presence within the healthcare consultant and broker ecosystem. The individual will conduct research to understand each firm's areas of influence, client base, priorities, and market position, using these insights to develop relevant and compelling engagement strategies. Working directly with the SVP, Channel Partnerships, this role will serve as a critical engine for expanding the consultant and broker channel pipeline. The BDR will maintain consistent engagement with prospective partners, coordinate meetings and introductions, track relationship progression, and ensure promising opportunities are appropriately qualified and advanced within the channel partnership process.  To work at Talkspace, you need to be as passionate as we are about our work, and excited to partner with us on delivering quality mental healthcare.

This is a remote position based on Eastern Time. Talkspace Headquarters is located in NYC.

What You’ll Do

• Consultant and Broker Relationship Development

• Build and maintain a strong network of relationships with healthcare consultants, brokers, advisors, and other influential industry stakeholders.

• Identify and engage key decision-makers, influencers, and relationship owners within national and regional consulting and brokerage firms.

• Establish the organization as a trusted and knowledgeable resource within the consultant and broker community.

• Develop relationships over time through consistent, thoughtful, and value-added engagement.

• Strategic Outreach and Business Development

• Develop and execute targeted outbound campaigns to consultant and broker organizations through email, phone, LinkedIn/social selling, events, networking, and other channels. 

• Research target firms, their areas of specialization, client portfolios, market priorities, and key stakeholders to create highly personalized outreach strategies.  

• Generate new conversations and qualified opportunities that align with the organization's growth and channel partnership objectives.  

• Leverage industry events, conferences, webinars, and other networking opportunities to expand the organization's consultant and broker relationships.  

• Opportunity Identification and Nurturing

• Identify emerging opportunities within consultant and broker organizations and proactively nurture relationships through the sales cycle.  

• Maintain consistent follow-up with prospects that are not yet sales-ready, keeping the organization top-of-mind for future client opportunities.  

• Understand consultant and broker influence within prospective accounts and identify opportunities where channel relationships can accelerate growth.  

• Coordinate introductions and discovery meetings between consultants/brokers and the appropriate internal sales or channel partnership leaders.  

• Maintain accurate and timely documentation of relationship activity, opportunities, next steps, and pipeline progression within CRM systems.  

• Channel Pipeline Development  

• Build and maintain a healthy pipeline of prospective consultant and broker relationships and opportunities.  

• Partner closely with the SVP, Channel Partnerships to prioritize target firms, develop account strategies, and determine appropriate engagement approaches.  

• Provide regular reporting on outreach activity, relationship development, pipeline progression, and emerging market opportunities.  

• Identify trends, competitive dynamics, and market intelligence gathered through consultant and broker interactions and communicate relevant insights to leadership.  

• Internal Collaboration  

• Collaborate with Channel Partnerships, Sales, Marketing, and other internal stakeholders to ensure coordinated engagement with consultant and broker partners.  

• Support preparation for consultant/broker meetings, presentations, industry events, and partnership discussions.  

• Help develop and refine messaging, materials, and engagement strategies designed specifically for the consultant and broker audience.  

• Support broader channel partnership initiatives and strategic growth priorities as directed by the SVP, Channel Partnerships.

• Performance & Results  

• Consistently achieve activity, relationship-development, qualified-opportunity, and pipeline-generation objectives.  

• Demonstrate disciplined follow-through and accountability in managing a large portfolio of prospective relationships.  

• Continuously test and refine outreach strategies to improve engagement, conversion, and channel pipeline performance.  

• Perform other related duties as assigned.  

About You 

• 2 - 5+ years of experience in healthcare, behavioral health, benefits, consulting, brokerage, business development, sales, or partnerships.  

• Experience working with or selling through healthcare consultants, benefits consultants, brokers, or other channel partners strongly preferred.  

• Demonstrated ability to develop relationships with senior stakeholders and build credibility within complex organizations.  

• Strong prospecting and business development skills, including experience with email, phone, LinkedIn/social selling, networking, and other outbound strategies.  

• Highly proactive, self-motivated, and comfortable independently managing a large portfolio of relationships and prospects.  

• Strong research and business acumen with the ability to understand an organization's business model, priorities, and key stakeholders.  

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to tailor messaging to different audiences.  

• Strong organizational and follow-up skills with the ability to manage multiple relationships and opportunities simultaneously.  

• Comfortable working in a fast-paced, dynamic environment where opportunities may develop over an extended period.  

• Goal-oriented and results-driven, with a strong commitment to building sustainable relationships rather than simply generating transactional leads.  

• Collaborative team player who thrives in a mission-driven environment.  

• Experience with Salesforce or other CRM platforms preferred.
